 SRI. G.M. ANANDA , ADVOCATE FOR R2,

1  THE ENDORSEMENT DTD 20.03.2023 BEARING NO.
 MY.NA/PRA/A.AA.SA.SHA/ENDORSEMENT/2022-23 ISSUED BY  THE R-2 VIDE ANNX-H TO THE WP AND CONSEQUENTLY  -2-  NC: 2023:KHC:20227
WP No. 7102 of 2023 DIRECT THE RESPONDENT TO ALLOT PLOT MEASURING 26838.0 SQ FEET IN THE SAME LAYOUT AS PRAYED IN THE REPRESENTATION DTD 15.03.2023 I.E ANNX-F IN COMPLIANCE WITH ORDER AT ANNX-D.

THIS WRIT PETITION COMING ON FOR PRELIMINARY HEARING IN 'B' GROUP THIS DAY, THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 ORDER
The petitioner and her children have succeeded to the property in Sy. No.157/1 measuring 2 acre 13 guntas situate at Hinkal Village, Kasaba Hobli, Mysore Taluk.
It is submitted that the 2nd respondent has formed Lay-out with respect to the petitioner's property without acquisition proceedings.

A suit came to be filed by the 1st petitioner and her children against the Mysore Urban Development Authority ('MUDA' for short).
2.

In the said suit, a compromise was entered into between the parties, which reads as follows:-
"TERMS AND CONDITIONS OF COMPROMISE PETITION"
1.
The plaintiffs are entitled to alternative land or site under the scheme of 50:50 ratio in respect of guntas of landed property situated at Hinkal Village, Kasaba Hobli, Mysuru Taluk.
On the basis of application fact, made enquiry, spot mahajar reports of the subordinates and also on the available documents and Gazette notifications.
It is confirmed that, in respect of the said plaint schedule property without passing any notifications and also without passing any award as provided under the law.
The said landed property utilized by authority for formation of layout.
The plaintiff also makes submission that the land has not been acquired under the Urban Land Ceiling Act.
3. The precedents in the similar fact in the case, on negotiation, the plaintiffs agreed to surrender their rights over the said property and the agreed to receive 50:50 ratio basis.
In interest of the authority and also based on the decision of the authority in similar cases.
It is persuaded the plaintiffs to get 50:50 ratio of developed sites in lieu of compensation.

sentences.text: 4. The plaintiff have furnished all the relevant revenue documents regarding the ownership and the genealogical trees issued by the Tahsildar, Mysuru Taluk,
are also discloses that the plaintiffs are legal heirs of RTC owner Puttathayamma.
Further, legal heirs of Puttathayamma shown in Genealogical tree executed a registered NC: 2023:KHC:20227 relinquishment deed in favour of Ningamma
thereby agreed and consented to proceed only in the name of Ningamma.

5. The plaintiffs also agreed to surrender/relinquish/give up their rights or what so ever over the said land to the authority, by agreeing to receive 50:50 ratio sites in lieu of compensation as full and final settlement and the plaintiffs further specifically agreed that they have no right to seek any monitory compensation and also the plaintiffs are not entitled for any enhanced compensation.
6. Both the parties have agreed to bare their own cost in the proceedings."
3. In terms of the said compromise entered into, the suit itself was disposed off and decree drawn-up on 20th February 2023.

The petitioner, pursuant to the settlement, has executed the relinquishment deed, which was approved by an order of MUDA dated 21.02.2023 whereby in terms of resolution of MUDA, the developed land of 26838.00 Sq.Ft. in the form of sites was agreed to be granted to the petitioner.

However, subsequently, an endorsement came to be issued on 20.03.2023 stating that in light of the Notification dated NC: 2023:KHC:20227 21.02.2023, no steps could be taken, in sofar as settlement arrived at with respect to the petitioner.
4.
It must be noticed that, compromise was entered into before the Civil Court in OS No.348/2020.

Once the decree has been drawn-up after the compromise petition having been accepted, the respondent-MUDA cannot wriggle out of legal consequences of compromise decree, as long as compromise decree subsists.

As no steps are taken to set aside the compromise decree as per law,
the same is to be valid for all purposes.
A compromise petition when accepted by the Court is deemed to be lawful and binds the parties.
As such, the legal consequences flowing from the compromise decree, the respondent-MUDA cannot resile from performing the commitments as contained in the compromise.
5. Perusal of the Government Circular dated 14.03.2023 would indicate that bar for granting of alternative land is prospective till guidelines are framed by the Government.
It is further clarified that the authority concerned would be responsible in sofar as acts already done in terms of the notification.

As the compromise has been entered into NC: 2023:KHC:20227 earlier, the Government Circular dated 14.03.2023 cannot be construed as a bar for giving effect to the compromise entered into in OS No.348/2020.
Accordingly, the endorsement is set aside.

The Respondent-MUDA shall comply with the terms and conditions contained in Compromise entered into between the parties in OS No. 348/2020.
6.
It is made clear that this order passed in the peculiar facts cannot be treated as precedent in other matters.

Accordingly, the petition is disposed off.
